_note: Collaboration logic shown when a card on the Head of Operations org chart is clicked. Only roles with a direct Head of Operations relationship have an entry; cards are matched by name first (to-be-hired and category cards), then by role. Optional labels override the panel headings.

CEO.owns: Company direction, major strategic decisions, senior leadership, investors and overall business performance.
CEO.works: Company priorities, organisational structure, business-wide visibility, major operational decisions and removing issues that do not need CEO involvement.
CEO.line: Operations removes operational complexity from the CEO and brings clear recommendations rather than raw problems.

Head of Operations.owns: How the business operates across people, systems, data and functions, with a focus on profitability, scalability and reducing unnecessary complexity.
Head of Operations.works: Operational performance and resource use, technology and data, organisational structure, People Operations, operational partners, compliance coordination and cross-functional company projects.
Head of Operations.line: Functional leaders own the results of their departments. Head of Operations builds the systems, controls and management infrastructure around them, fixes gaps between functions and takes operational complexity off the CEO’s plate.

Chief Financial Officer.owns: Financial reporting, cash, budgeting, accounting, banking, financial planning and the Finance team.
Chief Financial Officer.works: Connecting financial and operational data, resource and cost modelling, margin controls, forecasting, investment decisions and understanding the financial impact of operational changes.
Chief Financial Officer.line: Finance owns financial reporting and financial data. Operations owns the live operational data, systems and models used to understand what is happening before the financial result is final.

People Ops (HR).owns: Day-to-day People Operations, onboarding, performance processes, manager support, team engagement and employee/contractor administration.
People Ops (HR).works: Performance and accountability, what motivates different people, manager effectiveness, workforce planning, organisational gaps, onboarding, employment structures and making sure international employee and contractor arrangements are properly supported.
People Ops (HR).line: People Ops runs the day-to-day function. Head of Operations manages the function, sets priorities and remains accountable for its performance, working with legal or employment specialists where needed.

Technology Operations Associate.owns: Building, testing and maintaining internal systems, automations, integrations, data flows and operational tools.
Technology Operations Associate.works: Building internal software, connected data, forecasting and prediction models, automation, margin and capacity controls, open-source solutions and reducing software or manual operating cost.
Technology Operations Associate.line: Head of Operations defines the business problem, priorities and expected value. Technology Operations researches, builds, tests and maintains the technical solution.

Legal Consultant.owns: Specialist advice on contracts, employment and contractor structures, commercial agreements, compliance requirements and legal risk.
Legal Consultant.works: Making company processes legally workable, supporting international workforce structures, client compliance requirements, contracts with operational partners and identifying specialist support where needed.
Legal Consultant.line: Legal provides the specialist advice. Head of Operations makes sure the correct controls, owners and processes are put in place across the business.

Social Media Manager.owns: Day-to-day company social channels, content execution, publishing, community activity and agreed social performance targets.
Social Media Manager.works: Targets, reporting, processes, tools, productivity and making sure Social supports wider company priorities.
Social Media Manager.line: Head of Operations manages the function temporarily while there is no senior Marketing owner. The function moves under Marketing once the appropriate leadership layer is in place.

Head of Marketing + PR.owns: Overall company marketing, brand positioning, PR, communications and marketing strategy.
Head of Marketing + PR.works: Marketing systems, data and reporting, resources, technology, cross-functional projects and the transition of functions temporarily managed by Operations.
Head of Marketing + PR.line: Marketing owns the strategy and results. Operations helps build the infrastructure and removes operational blockers.

Chief Sales Officer.owns: Sales strategy, revenue targets, Sales leadership, pipeline performance and overall new business performance.
Chief Sales Officer.works: Pipeline and forecasting data, CRM infrastructure, lead flow, sales capacity, automation and understanding what expected revenue means for Delivery, hiring and company resources.
Chief Sales Officer.line: Chief Sales Officer owns revenue generation. Operations makes sure the business has the systems, information and capacity to support that growth.

Director of New Business.owns: New business strategy, major opportunities, lead generation channels and improving how the company wins new clients.
Director of New Business.works: Lead-generation infrastructure, pipeline data, CRM, forecasting, automation, new commercial channels and understanding what future business means operationally.
Director of New Business.line: New Business owns generating and converting opportunities. Operations builds the infrastructure that helps it scale.

Client Director.owns: Senior client relationships, strategic account growth, commercial performance and oversight of key accounts and Account Managers.
Client Director.works: Client and revenue forecasting, account targets, reporting infrastructure, team structure and recurring issues that require several departments to work together.
Client Director.line: Client Director owns client strategy and account performance. Operations supports the structure, data and accountability around it.

Head of Delivery and Performance.owns: Delivery performance, campaign margin, quality, timelines, capacity and performance of the Delivery team.
Head of Delivery and Performance.works: Margin-control systems, capacity and forecasting models, resource planning, Delivery data, automation and identifying recurring problems that need a structural fix.
Head of Delivery and Performance.line: Head of Delivery owns Delivery results. Head of Operations builds the company-level controls, data and infrastructure that help Delivery achieve those results and give leadership visibility.

Senior Campaign Managers.owns: Performance of the campaigns under their responsibility, including margin, timelines, quality, risk and Campaign Manager performance.
Senior Campaign Managers.works: Margin controls, capacity, workload allocation, performance data, process improvements and recurring Delivery issues.
Senior Campaign Managers.line: Senior Campaign Managers own the results of their campaigns. Until a Head of Delivery is in place, Operations provides an additional layer of visibility and control around those results.

Operational Partners & Specialists.owns: Fulfilment centres, production partners, logistics providers, specialist platforms, compliance providers and other external resources required to deliver campaigns.
Operational Partners & Specialists.works: Finding the right partners, comparing cost and capability, negotiating better operating setups and making sure there is a clear internal owner and process.
Operational Partners & Specialists.line: The relevant functional team uses the partner day to day. Operations owns the wider setup, efficiency and commercial structure where the relationship affects multiple teams or the operating model.
